stem: BC is a tangent at B and AB is a chord, cutting off an arc AB of 130° (the other arc is 230°). The angle of tangency ∠ABC equals the inscribed angle on the same arc. Calculate $m(\angle ABC)$: drag A, B and C so that the inscribed angle ∠ACB, facing the 130° arc, has the same measure as ∠ABC.
solution: The angle ABC is an angle of tangency; the arc between its sides is the 130° arc AB (not the 230° arc).
An angle of tangency is half the measure of the arc between its sides.
It equals the inscribed angle on the same arc, so set the inscribed angle to 65°.

hints.text: The arc is not the angle. An angle of tangency or inscribed angle on an arc is only a fraction of that arc's measure.
Check which arc lies between the sides of the angle of tangency; the angle must face that arc.
Take the arc between the sides of the angle and use the rule connecting an angle of tangency with its arc.

notes: Angle of tangency equals inscribed angle on the same arc; the widget builds that inscribed angle. Matches book answer 65.
